newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Local H1 profit up 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Credit Local H1 profit up 6 pct.

text.p: (Figures in millions of French francs unless stated)

NOTE - French bank Credit Local de France chairman Pierre Richard, forecasting a rise in 1996 profits, said in a statement: "On the eve of of our alliance with Credit Communal de Belgique (CCB), Credit Local de France is displaying its strength.

"Its financial results are very satisfactory and our commercial activity during the first eight months has been sustained, especially in the international sector which is developing strongly," he said.
CLF, like CCB, specialises in offering loans to local and regional public authorities.
CLF said operating costs rose 15.7 percent, mainly due to integration of four new units, including CLF-Hypothekenbank Berlin and CLF-Suede.
Provisions included 96 million francs for real estate against 136 million in the first half of 1995 and a nine million franc net recovery of provisions.
Corporate taxes rose 34 percent due to the increase in gross operating profit and consolidation of companies paying tax.
The group will pay a gross exceptional dividend of 25.50 francs per share or 17 francs net to shareholders before the alliance with CCB on top of a 20.85 franc gross dividend paid in June 1996.

The bank had said last July that it would pay a total exceptional dividend of 626 million francs to shareholders before the alliance went into effect. The dividend payment is aimed at redressing the difference in size between the two banks.
The alliance in which the two banks plan to take cross-holdings in each other's share capital, will come into effect at the end of the year, creating the 22nd largest bank in Europe.
